choices: Its projection along a chosen axis

questions.question: What is dimensional analysis?
choices: Counting only the digits in an instrument reading
Checking relationships using the dimensions of physical quantities

questions.question: Which dimension is represented by speed?
Which unit combination represents acceleration?
In a velocity-time graph, what does signed area represent?
Why must a direction convention be stated when reporting signed velocity?
choices: A positive or negative sign refers to the chosen axis
Velocity can be measured without any reference

questions.question: Why can total distance differ from displacement magnitude?
choices: Displacement counts every step without direction
A path can include motion in different directions
They always use different length units

questions.question: What does a line's intercept represent in a position-time model x = x0 + vt?
choices: The change in position per unit time
The time when velocity first reaches zero

questions.question: Why is a formula with meters on one side and seconds on the other suspect?
choices: The symbols must be spelled identically on both sides
The numbers alone establish correctness even with mismatched dimensions
Both sides must always represent a vector

questions.question: Why should repeated measurements be reported with their spread as well as their average?
choices: The average becomes meaningless in every case
The spread shows variability not visible in the average
Spread gives the exact true value
Repeated readings remove every systematic error

questions.question: Why should a measured value include units?
choices: Units determine the correct result without a measurement
The number alone does not specify its physical scale

questions.question: How can changing from meters to centimeters affect a reported length?
choices: The numerical value changes but the physical length does not

questions.question: What does a curved position-time graph indicate about motion?
choices: The velocity changes as the slope changes
The velocity is constant because time keeps increasing
The position is the same at every time
The slope always represents acceleration instead of velocity
